items.text: Page title [27] Keyword Agent
Section: AI Agents
Page [27] Keyword Agent scope: MVP.
Page URL .../page/keyword-agent
The Keyword Agent generates search terms optimized for marketplace discovery.
The Keyword Agent generates backend keywords optimized for marketplace discovery.
Keywords: keyword agent, search terms, backend keywords, SEO, search, discovery
Purpose
The Keyword Agent generates discovery-optimized search terms and backend keywords.
Keyword Agent focuses on what shoppers actually search for, not keyword stuffing.
Backend keywords are Amazon-specific.
Backend keywords are terms that don't appear in the listing.
Backend keywords help with search visibility.
Inputs & Outputs
Table header: Input | Source
Keyword Agent input: Category, sourced from Category mapping.
Keyword Agent input: Product attributes, sourced from Product table.
Keyword Agent input: Marketplace, sourced from Target marketplace.
Keyword Agent input: Existing search signals, sourced from Performance data.
Performance data as source of existing search signals for Keyword Agent is Phase 3.
Keyword Agent input: Brand terminology, sourced from Brand glossary chunks.
Keyword Agent output: search_terms (array).
Keyword Agent output: backend_keywords (array).
Keyword Agent output: keyword_recommendations (optional).
Validation Rules
Keyword validation rule: No keyword stuffing.
Keyword validation rule: each term must be semantically distinct.
Backend keywords must not duplicate visible listing content (Amazon rule).
No competitor brand names in keywords.
Marketplace-specific keyword length limits respected.
Amazon backend keyword limit: 250 bytes total.
Non-Technical Explanation
Keyword Agent figures out what words shoppers use to find products like yours; like an SEO specialist who knows exactly how Amazon and Flipkart search works.
Marketplaces penalize stuffing irrelevant keywords; Keyword Agent generates search-friendly terms without stuffing.

Page title [28] Attribute Agent
Section: AI Agents
Page [28] Attribute Agent scope: MVP.
Page URL .../page/attribute-agent
The Attribute Agent maps product information to marketplace-specific structured attributes.
The Attribute Agent handles category schemas.
The Attribute Agent handles marketplace field differences.
Keywords: attribute agent, structured attributes, category schema, mapping, color, material, size
Purpose
The Attribute Agent converts product information into marketplace-specific structured attributes.
Each marketplace has its own category schema.
Marketplace category schemas have different attribute names.
Marketplace category schemas have different allowed values.
Marketplace category schemas have different requirements.
Marketplace Mapping Example
Table header: Canonical | Amazon | Flipkart
Canonical attribute example: color = "navy blue".
Amazon mapping of canonical color: Color = "Navy".
Flipkart mapping of canonical color: Colour = "Navy Blue".
Canonical attribute example: material = "organic cotton".
Amazon mapping of canonical material: Material = "Cotton".
Flipkart mapping of canonical material: Fabric = "Organic Cotton".
Canonical attribute example: size = "L".
Amazon mapping of canonical size: Size = "Large".
Flipkart mapping of canonical size: Size = "L".
Engineering Notes
Architecture Decision
Marketplace-specific attribute mapping belongs inside marketplace adapters / mapping layers, NOT spread throughout the AI system.
The Attribute Agent generates canonical attributes.
The adapter maps canonical attributes to marketplace-specific formats.
Keeping attribute mapping in adapters / mapping layers keeps marketplace logic contained.
Missing attributes are flagged in the ErrorReport with source "rules_engine".
Missing attributes are flagged with error code "MISSING_ATTRIBUTE".
Category mismatch (product doesn't fit the selected category schema) is flagged as "CATEGORY_MISMATCH".

Page title [29] Image Agent
Section: AI Agents
Page [29] Image Agent scope: MVP.
Page URL .../page/image-agent
The Image Agent validates product images against marketplace requirements.
Image validation uses deterministic checks.
Image validation uses vision model analysis.
Keywords: image agent, image compliance, vision, background, resolution, watermark
Image Pipeline
The Image Agent runs a compliance pipeline on every product image.
The Image Agent compliance pipeline is two-stage.
mermaid graph TD fence
Image pipeline: IMG "Product Image" --> S3 "Upload to S3".
Product images are uploaded to S3 as the first step of the image pipeline, before deterministic checks.
Image pipeline: S3 "Upload to S3" --> DET "Deterministic Checks".
Image pipeline: DET "Deterministic Checks" --> VIS "Vision Model Review".
Image pipeline: VIS "Vision Model Review" --> RPT "ImageReport per image per slot".
An ImageReport is produced per image per slot.
Image pipeline: RPT --> PASS {"Pass?"} decision.
Image pipeline "Pass?" decision outcomes: "Yes" or "Fail/Warn" (pass, fail, warn).
Image pipeline: PASS -->|"Yes"| ATTACH "Attach to listing".
Image pipeline: PASS -->|"Fail/Warn"| SURFACE "Surface issue + suggestion".
mermaid closing fence
Check Types
Table header: Check | Amazon | Flipkart | Method
Amazon main image background: Pure white RGB(255,255,255).
Flipkart main image background: White/light.
Main image background check method: Programmatic pixel analysis.
Main image background check method: vision confirmation.
Amazon minimum resolution: 1000×1000 px (zoom).
Flipkart minimum resolution: 500 px min.
Flipkart resolution: 1000 recommended.
Minimum resolution check method: Deterministic (PIL/exif).
Amazon product fill ratio: ≥ 85% of frame.
Flipkart product fill ratio: — (no requirement stated).
Product fill ratio check method: Vision model.
Amazon text overlays / watermarks: Not allowed on main image.
Flipkart text overlays / watermarks: Restricted.
Text overlays / watermarks check method: Vision model.
Amazon logo / branding: Only product logo on product itself.
Flipkart logo / branding: Same (only product logo on product itself).
Logo / branding check method: Vision model.
Amazon aspect ratio: 1:1 main.
Amazon aspect ratio: others vary by slot.
Flipkart aspect ratio: 1:1 (of "1:1 and 3:4").
Flipkart aspect ratio: 3:4 (of "1:1 and 3:4").
Aspect ratio check method: Deterministic.

Page title [30] Brand Voice Agent / Retrieval
Section: AI Agents
Page [30] Brand Voice Agent / Retrieval scope: MVP.
Page URL .../page/brand-voice-agent
Brand Voice Retrieval: brand tone is vectorized.
Brand Voice Retrieval: vectorized brand tone, style, glossary and compliance rules are injected into agent prompts.
Brand Voice Retrieval: brand style is vectorized.
Brand Voice Retrieval: brand glossary is vectorized.
Brand Voice Retrieval: brand compliance rules are vectorized.
Keywords: brand voice, retrieval, pgvector, embedding, tone, style, glossary
What Gets Vectorized
Table header: Artifact | Chunking | Example Content
Vectorized artifact: Brand voice guide, chunked Per rule / tone clause.
Brand voice guide example content: "Playful, not corporate. Use 'you' not 'the customer'."
Vectorized artifact: Style preferences, chunked Per guideline.
Style preferences example content: "Never use exclamation marks. Bullets start with verbs."
Vectorized artifact: Glossary / terminology, chunked Per term.
Glossary / terminology example content: "Say 'kurta set' not 'kurta outfit'."
Vectorized artifact: Past approved listings, chunked Per listing field.
Past approved listings example content: High-performing titles, bullets, descriptions.
Vectorized artifact: Compliance preferences, chunked Per rule.
Compliance preferences example content: "Never claim 'organic' without certification."
Brand voice retrieval happens at generation time ("Retrieval at Generation Time").
mermaid graph TD fence
Retrieval input REQ "Generation request" carries: product.
Retrieval input REQ "Generation request" carries: brand_id.
Retrieval input REQ "Generation request" carries: marketplace.
Retrieval step EMB: Embed the request context.
Retrieval step PGV: "pgvector cosine-similarity search" (pgvector used for retrieval).
Brand voice retrieval: top-k = 8.
Retrieval step PGV similarity metric: cosine-similarity.
Retrieval step INJECT: Inject retrieved chunks into agent prompt.
Retrieval step GEN: Agent generates text conditioned on voice + rules.
Retrieval sequence: REQ --> EMB --> PGV --> INJECT --> GEN.
mermaid closing fence
Default embedding model: text-embedding-3-small.
The embedding model choice is a configuration, not an architecture decision.
The embedding model is swappable without architectural changes.

Page title [31] Optimization Agent
Section: AI Agents
Page [31] Optimization Agent scope: PHASE3.
Page URL .../page/optimization-agent
The Optimization Agent analyzes performance data.
The Optimization Agent proposes improvements to existing listings.
The Optimization Agent runs on schedule, not continuously.
Keywords: optimization agent, performance, improvement, scheduled, CTR, conversion
Purpose
Optimization Agent consumes performance metric: impressions.
Optimization Agent consumes performance metric: clicks.
Optimization Agent consumes performance metric: conversions.
Optimization Agent consumes performance metric: returns.
Optimization Agent consumes performance metric: ranking.
Optimization Agent proposes changes to existing listings.
Optimization Agent identifies underperforming listings.
Optimization Agent analyzes patterns in high-performing listings.
Optimization Agent suggests specific field-level improvements.
Trigger Model
Scheduled, Not Continuous
Optimization Agent runs on a schedule (e.g., weekly), not continuously.
On schedule, Optimization Agent analyzes accumulated performance data.
On schedule, Optimization Agent generates optimization proposals.
Scheduled (not continuous) trigger is critical for cost efficiency.
Continuous optimization would be expensive and unnecessary.
Optimization Agent input: Performance metrics per listing per marketplace.
Optimization Agent output: Proposed changes to existing listings: title.
Optimization Agent output: Proposed changes to existing listings: bullets.
Optimization Agent output: Proposed changes to existing listings: keywords.
Optimization proposals go through the same validation → approval pipeline as new listings.

Page title [32] Future Agent Registry
Section: AI Agents
Page [32] Future Agent Registry scope: FUTURE.
Page URL .../page/future-agent-registry
New agents can be registered and integrated into the platform without rewriting core infrastructure.
Keywords: agent registry, future agents, extensibility, plugin, registration
Registry Design
Agent registry pattern allows new agents to be added without modifying the core orchestration layer.
Each agent implements a standard interface.
python code fence
class AgentInterface(ABC) is the standard agent interface.
Docstring: "Standard interface for all agents."
AgentInterface field: name: str.
AgentInterface field: version: str.
AgentInterface field: scope: str, values "mvp" | "phase2" | "phase3" | "future".
AgentInterface abstract method: async def execute(self, context: AgentContext) -> AgentOutput.
AgentInterface abstract method: def get_input_schema(self) -> dict.
AgentInterface abstract method: def get_output_schema(self) -> dict.
code fence close
New agents register with the orchestrator.
New agents plug into the existing data layer.
New agents plug into the existing validation pipeline.
New agents plug into the existing observability infrastructure.
Registry is how the Listing Agent can expand into the full Marketplace OS without platform rewrites.

Page title [35] Canonical Listing Model
Section: Listing Generation
Page [35] Canonical Listing Model scope: MVP.
Page URL .../page/canonical-listing-model
The canonical listing representation is marketplace-independent.
The canonical listing is the core data contract between AI agents and marketplace adapters.
Keywords: canonical, listing model, marketplace independent, JSON schema
Canonical Schema
Canonical Listing
json code fence and opening brace
Canonical listing field: "listing_id" (example "list_789").
Canonical listing field: "product_id" (example "prod_456").
Canonical listing field: "marketplace" (example "amazon").
Canonical listing field: "category" (example "ethnic_wear_kurta_sets").
Canonical listing field: "status" (example "generated").
Canonical listing field: "content" object.
Canonical listing content field: "title" (string).
Canonical listing content field: "bullets" (array of strings).
Canonical listing content field: "description" (string).
closing brace },
Canonical listing field: "keywords" object.
Canonical listing keywords field: "search_terms" (array of strings).
Canonical listing keywords field: "backend_keywords" (array of strings).
closing brace },
Canonical listing field: "attributes" object.
Canonical listing attribute example: "color": "navy blue".
Canonical listing attribute example: "material": "organic cotton".
Canonical listing attribute example: "size": "L".
closing brace },
Canonical listing field: "image_reports" (array, example []).
Canonical listing field: "confidence_score" (example 0.87).
Canonical listing field: "version" (example 1).
Canonical listing field: "created_at" (example "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z").
closing brace and code fence
Why Canonical
The canonical model is marketplace-independent.
The canonical model does not contain Amazon-specific field names.
The canonical model does not contain Flipkart-specific formats.
The canonical model does not contain any raw marketplace API structures.
Marketplace-specific mapping happens inside adapters.
Adding a new marketplace requires only a new adapter, not changes to the core data model.
Invariant
Invariant: Marketplace-specific fields never appear in the canonical listing model.
The canonical model is the shared contract between Intelligence and Execution layers.
